name: warp
resume: All three exports are done. Distances, change points, and boundaries match warp, including a zoned POSIXct. NumPy holds the columns. zoneinfo supplies the civil date.

functions.name: warp_distance
functions.done: Distances from an origin, counted in period groups.

check.case: Month, yday, mweek, clock hour, UTC milliseconds, and a New York year.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(warp))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jsonlite))
x <- as.Date("2016-01-01") + 0:400
x[10] <- NA
origin <- as.Date("2016-03-01")
px <- as.POSIXct(c(0, 3600.5, 86400, 1.3e9), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
ny <- as.POSIXct(c(0, 18000, 86400), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "America/New_York")
json_val <- function(value) {
  toJSON(as.numeric(value), auto_unbox = FALSE, digits = 17, na = "null")
}

one <- function() {
  
c(
  warp_distance(x, "month", every = 2L, origin = origin),
  warp_distance(x, "yday", every = 7L),
  warp_distance(x, "mweek"),
  warp_distance(x, "hour", every = 5L),
  warp_distance(px, "millisecond", every = 10L),
  warp_distance(ny, "year")
)

}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (step_i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[step_i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf('{"value":%s,"median_ms":%.17g}\n', json_val(value), median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import json, statistics, time

import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
import numpy as np
from warp import Date, POSIXct, warp_distance
days = [date(2016, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(401)]
days[9] = None
x = Date(days)
origin = Date("2016-03-01")
px = POSIXct([0, 3600.5, 86400, 1.3e9], "UTC")
ny = POSIXct([0, 18000, 86400], "America/New_York")

def one():
    parts = [
        warp_distance(x, "month", every=2, origin=origin),
        warp_distance(x, "yday", every=7),
        warp_distance(x, "mweek"),
        warp_distance(x, "hour", every=5),
        warp_distance(px, "millisecond", every=10),
        warp_distance(ny, "year"),
    ]
    out = []
    for part in parts:
        for value in np.asarray(part).tolist():
            if isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value):
                out.append(None)
            else:
                out.append(value)
    return out

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))

import json, statistics, time

import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
import numpy as np
from warp import Date, warp_change
days = [date(2016, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(401)]
days[9] = None
x = Date(days)

def one():
    parts = [
        warp_change(x, "month"),
        warp_change(x, "yday", every=10, last=False, endpoint=True),
    ]
    out = []
    for part in parts:
        out.extend(np.asarray(part).tolist())
    return out

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))

import json, statistics, time

import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
import numpy as np
from warp import Date, warp_boundary
days = [date(2016, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(401)]
days[9] = None
x = Date(days)
origin = Date("2016-03-01")

def one():
    boundary = warp_boundary(x, "day", every=5, origin=origin)
    return np.asarray(boundary.start).tolist() + np.asarray(boundary.stop).tolist()

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))
